arena: Classic Generic procedural_v2 11x9 two-player, native replanned three-turn search at every atomic action, action limit2400

fixed_window.sample_rule: First live decision of each seat during exact native-replanned self-play

verification: Every indexed completed-turn plan replayed exactly to its native static score. The existing full Python suite passed 491 tests and Ruff passed on one low-priority pinned SSH-server CPU. Rust, Python and web CI passed for the code commit. No model was trained or used to select a move.
interpretation: The proposed full-spatial candidate pipeline is about 8.8 times slower at these easy first-seat states than the already-strong native three-turn search. One cold encoder call dominates p95, but the warm median alone fails the fixed gate. These first decisions do not represent later crowded states, so this is a narrow interface/runtime no-go, not a claim that all neural process models or later-game inference are too slow. Do not retune the predeclared gate or train a selector from this failed feasibility window.
next: Seek a structurally different process compression with a credible per-action runtime budget before fresh, fully disjoint fit/calibration/offline/game/final data. Keep the rejected episode-preference checkpoint rejected and its reserved game seeds untouched. Any future promotion needs fresh complete both-seat independent-map games versus the frozen direct model and native replanned teacher plus runtime/profile gates.
